goal: Lackluster Plus+ is a running TV-channels web app: one page (public/index.html, about 3,000 lines) with a channel guide and a player, served by a small Node gateway. It works with a mouse or a finger. This plan makes the whole page usable with a TV remote (arrow keys, OK, Back), so it can run on a Fire TV stick and on TCL Fire TVs. All of it goes into ONE new file, public/tvnav.js, loaded by one new script tag; nothing else in the app changes, and mouse and touch keep working exactly as before.
rules: All new code goes in public/tvnav.js. public/index.html gets exactly one new line (the script tag) and nothing else in it changes. dist/ does not change at all.
Mouse and touch keep working exactly as before. On a computer nothing looks or behaves differently until an arrow key is pressed.
The highlight is real keyboard focus (element.focus()), never a painted box that is not focus: the page's own code and the TV's screen reader rely on focus.
Never open a window or a new tab, and never highlight a link that would (target="_blank").
Names, ids, class names and exact strings are the ones in the brief and the tests. Where the brief gives a function 'exactly', copy it as it is: it was tuned against the real page in a real browser.
The brand stays: Lackluster Plus+, Philibert TV by Esteef.Ai, as the page shows it now.
conventions: public/tvnav.js: plain browser JavaScript in one (function(){ 'use strict'; ... })(); two-space indents, single quotes, var and function (no modules, no build, no libraries).
Run a task's test with: .venv\Scripts\python.exe tests\<file>.py (it prints PASS/FAIL lines and starts the server and a headless browser itself).
Scratch files and experiments go in the system temp folder, never in the project folder.
